Chapter 1: Rediscovering Awe in a World That Forgets
You know how easy it is for life to settle into a rhythm—where days start to blend together, and the things that once felt mysterious or even magical, just sort of fade into the background? Sometimes, in those quiet moments, maybe you feel a subtle emptiness. Like, something important has slipped out of view, and you can’t quite put your finger on it. It happens a lot when we think about God. For so many people, the idea of God has become, well... familiar. Almost too familiar. The words and traditions of faith are still there, but that sense of wonder? It’s not as strong as it used to be.
Picture a small church on a Wednesday evening. People gather for a midweek service. The prayers are heartfelt, and the songs ring out, but there’s this heaviness—almost like everyone’s just going through the motions. Someone sits quietly in the back, remembering a time when just thinking about God filled them with awe. Worship used to feel like standing on the edge of something huge and mysterious. But now? God feels distant. Ordinary, even.
And honestly, this quiet sense of loss isn’t rare. In so many communities, that feeling of God’s majesty has faded. Gradually, we trade in the overwhelming for something that’s easier to handle. It’s comfortable, but it’s also less demanding. The change is subtle, but it really matters. Because when God becomes just another part of life—helpful, sure, but not truly awe-inspiring—faith loses its power to change us. The heart grows numb, and worship turns into a routine.
Most of the time, you don’t even notice it happening. It’s like a slow leak in a tire. The pressure slips away bit by bit, and before you know it, the ride’s rough and uncertain. The real issue isn’t with the rituals or the words. It’s what happens when our vision of God shrinks. When we reduce Him to a distant helper, or just a vague idea, the foundation of faith starts to crack.
So, what’s the way forward? It’s not about adding more activities or chasing after the next big thing. It’s about something deeper: recovering a true sense of who God really is—His greatness, His mystery, His holiness. And this isn’t just about having the right beliefs; it’s about meeting the deepest need of the heart. Because when you start to see God as He truly is, everything else finds its place. Worship becomes alive again, life feels meaningful, and your soul can finally rest.
It all starts with a simple, but powerful question: What comes to mind when you think about God? For most of us, those first thoughts are shaped by childhood memories, cultural images, maybe even our own wishes. But let’s be honest—those ideas often fall short. The real challenge is letting go of the small, comfortable notions, and opening ourselves up to the possibility that God is so much greater—and more mysterious—than we could ever imagine.
